prize_parts.citation: for the development of targeted protein degradation, in which small molecules recruit ubiquitin ligases to destroy chosen proteins

statement.case_for: I have changed my preferred configuration from a two-part prize (B050 Liu plus B052 Cullis and Hope) to a single part on targeted protein degradation. In round 1 I said I would move B042 above lipid nanoparticles if a single defensible citation could be shown, and the exchange has supplied one: a small molecule that induces proximity between an E3 ligase and a chosen protein, so that the cell's own ubiquitin-proteasome machinery removes the target. Crews and Deshaies conceived and demonstrated the bifunctional version in 2001, and Handa's identification of cereblon as the thalidomide target gave the glue strand its molecular mechanism. Both strands act through the same principle, and a physicist can state it quantitatively as control of ternary-complex equilibria and of catalytic, sub-stoichiometric turnover. It opens a capability that occupancy-based inhibitors lack, and that generative potential is what I look for. Six members ranked it in the openings, five list it as a preferred configuration or alternative, and it is the only candidate most members can accept as a second choice. It also sits cleanly in chemistry, which answers the objection I raised against my own pairing: two nucleic-acid-medicine parts could read as Chemistry following Medicine.
statement.case_against: The attribution is the weak point. Three seats exclude Ciulli (VHL ligands and ternary-complex design), Gray, Sakamoto, Kim and Ito, each with a credible claim, and the first PROTACs were peptidic and cell-impermeable, so the step to drug-like degraders came from other hands. No PROTAC drug is yet approved, so the consequence is promissory, whereas lipid nanoparticles (B052) already underpin approved products at global scale and base editing (B050) has reached patients. I may be underweighting maturity because I am pulled by the principle. If the expert reports show that the PROTAC and glue strands are two achievements, the citation would have to be narrowed and my preference would revert to B052 or B050.

responses.point: Aqvist ranks targeted protein degradation first as a simple chemical idea, recruiting E3 ligases with bifunctional molecules or glues, and proposes Crews, Deshaies and Handa, while conceding that PROTACs and glues may be two lineages and that approved drugs are few.
responses.response: You asked, in effect, for the same thing I asked in round 1, a single citation, and I now think your wording supplies it: recruiting an E3 ligase to a chosen protein is the shared principle, and cereblon explains why thalidomide-type glues belong to it. I have therefore adopted your three names. I accept your point that the clinical record is promissory and I do not hide it. I would still want the citation to say 'recruit' rather than 'develop drugs', so that it honours the concept and does not depend on an approval that has not happened.

responses.point: Brzezinski prefers B042 with Crews, Deshaies and Handa, argues that Handa is the natural third name because the cereblon target explains the glue strand, and asks that the expert reports state what remains unsettled on ternary complexes and the absence of an approved PROTAC.
responses.response: I agree with your reasoning on Handa and with the request to the expert reports, and I would make it a condition of the vote that they state clearly what is settled and what is not. Your point that the first PROTAC molecules were peptidic and impermeable is the strongest argument for Ciulli, and I take it seriously. It leaves me choosing between crediting the originating concept (Crews, Deshaies) plus the mechanism of the glue strand (Handa), or the later drug-like design. I choose the former because the committee has usually honoured the first demonstration of a principle, but I recognise that this is a judgement, not a settled fact.

responses.point: Chabes prefers base editing with Liu, Komor and Gaudelli, but says his preference would give way to a more clearly chemical modality such as B042 if base editing is judged to be medicine or biotechnology.
responses.response: I share your concern, and it is the reason I have moved. The 2020 CRISPR prize makes base editing a harder argument for a decade-old field, and as chair I cannot dismiss the view that it will be read as biotechnology. On trainee credit I stay where I was in round 1: Liu alone is the cleanest attribution, but if the committee wants three names for this topic your Liu, Komor and Gaudelli is the better version. I would ask you directly whether you can accept B042 as your preferred configuration, since you named it as an alternative and you said that a chemical framing would decide the matter for you.

responses.point: Aili prefers ionizable lipid nanoparticles with Cullis, Hope and Anderson, citing the pKa-tuned charge switch, approved products at global scale and a transferable design principle, and notes the 2023 Medicine overlap.
responses.response: Your maturity argument is the best case against my new position, because approved lipid-nanoparticle medicines are real and degraders are not yet approved. My answer is that the 2023 Medicine prize overlap and the unresolved Vancouver-Boston split make B052 harder to word as chemistry, and the chair's question on credit has not been answered by anyone: nobody has said whether Hope, Madden or Anderson has the strongest claim on the ionizable-lipid concept. I keep B052 as my first alternative, and if you can show that Cullis, Hope and Anderson is a defensible and stable attribution I would weigh it level with B042.

responses.point: Sparr prefers biomolecular phase separation with Hyman, Brangwynne and Rosen as a physical-chemical organising principle, and concedes that its in vivo generality is disputed and that she may overvalue it as a soft-matter specialist.
responses.response: I appreciate that you stated the weakness of your own case. My difficulty remains that the citation would have to say what is established about organisation in living cells, and the disagreement over artefacts and generality makes that sentence hard to write precisely. I did not move toward B024 in this round, but I would like to hear which specific measurement, for example the multivalency phase diagrams, you regard as beyond dispute, because that is the only form in which I could support it.

uncertainties: Whether the expert reports will show that PROTACs and molecular glues are one achievement or two, which decides whether Handa belongs in the citation
Whether the absence of an approved PROTAC drug is enough to put B042 behind B052 on demonstrated consequence
Whether Crews, Deshaies and Handa is a fair three-name cut given Ciulli, Gray, Sakamoto, Kim and Ito
Whether the committee will treat base editing as chemistry given the 2020 CRISPR prize, and whether lipid nanoparticles read as a second recognition of the 2023 mRNA work
statement.conflict_note: No specific conflict is apparent from my profile for any shortlisted candidate. I am at Lund University with committee colleagues Somfai and Sparr, but none of the shortlisted candidates is connected to Lund or to my own research group, and nothing in this round changes that disclosure.
